title: Length of Last Word
corePattern: Reverse Traversal / String Parsing from End
interviewTips: Ask if input can have leading, trailing, or multiple consecutive spaces — e.g., 'Hello World   ' vs '   fly me   to   the moon  '.
Trade-off: split() is concise but uses O(n) extra space for words array; reverse scan is O(1) space and optimal — mention this proactively.
Edge-case tip: single word with no spaces, all spaces constraint-wise not possible but trailing spaces are guaranteed test; ensure you skip trailing spaces first then count.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Split and Take Last
approaches.intuition: A word is defined as maximal non-space characters. If we split the string by spaces, the answer is simply the length of the last token. Python split() and C++ stringstream operator>> and Java trim+split automatically ignore extra spaces.
approaches.theory: Tokenize the string on whitespace delimiter. Let tokens be t0..tk-1 after discarding empty tokens caused by multiple spaces. By definition last word is tk-1, so answer is len(tk-1). Scanning for delimiters is linear, but storing all tokens costs extra space proportional to input.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single pass over n characters to find delimiters and build tokens. n = s.length().

spaceComplexity.explanation: Stores split words array / tokens in worst case (e.g., single word or many words) copying O(n) characters.

edgeCases: Trailing spaces: 'Hello World   ' -> split ignores empties, last='World' -> 5

approaches.name: Approach 2: Reverse Scan with Two Phases
approaches.intuition: We only need the last word, so start from the end. First skip trailing spaces, then count characters until next space or start of string. No splitting or extra storage needed.
approaches.theory: Let i = n-1. Invariant 1: suffix (i+1..n-1) is all spaces to skip. Decrement i while s[i]==' '. Invariant 2: now i points at end of last word. Count len while i>=0 and s[i]!=' ', decrementing i. When loop stops, len equals maximal non-space suffix length, which is definition of last word length.

timeComplexity.explanation: At most one backward pass over n characters; worst case single word scans whole string, best case short last word is O(k) where k is trailing spaces + last word length.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two integer pointers/counters, no copy of string or token array.

dryRunExample.input: s = '   fly me   to   the moon  '
steps: i=26 at end, skip trailing spaces -> i=25 at 'n' of moon
count: m-o-o-n -> len=1,2,3,4, i moves to space before moon

edgeCases: Trailing spaces: 'Hello World   ' -> skip 3 spaces then count 5
Leading spaces + one word: '   a' -> skip 0 trailing, count 1
